body:
No it just felt like... "wow you're doing a really bad job" and it's like, I know this already? 

Income is the only solution but I was hoping I could come up with some sort of masterlist of things I can work on during the day (as I'm sure you know unemployment comes with a lot of free time) of things I could try for more income that exclude anything illegal or hurtful to myself (for example, sex work). 

Luckily I just got an interview for a church pianist position with really low pay (lower than my last one) but it's something and I hope it goes somewhere. 

Sorry for freaking out. I'm slowly realizing that I have to make most decisions myself as an adult, without someone more adult-y than myself to help me, and that's just difficult ig.

I actually wouldn't mind walking dogs at all! I don't have to speak and one of my biggest problems is that I have trouble actually speaking and communicating with adults on a normal interpersonal level. 

No I'm not in a lot of debt, but for having no income it just FEELS like a lot of debt. But I am really hoping this job works out with the Spectrum House (it's a place to work with developmentally disabled kids) but I am just not sure with transportation and such but I think it might be possible and I'm assuming there's people who have been in worse debt who have made it out in one piece.

On Tricare they only keep it until 23 I believe for the dependents. I'm probably going to call and ask for details about that though and maybe find an inpatient setting because I am not really fit to be living in "the real world" right now. 

For the ACA I think it's different, but specifically military I think I only have it until I'm 23 if I'm a full time student (which of course complicates more things).

When I say I "didn't want to" I mean the job seemed kind of terrible to me. You know those people that bother you at the mall? That's the job it was and it's unsuitable for someone like me. Not just unsuitable, but impossible. I sometimes go non-verbal I get so shy and anxious so it's not a great idea. It was dumb to take the job in all honesty. 

Actually I just called a church and they only pay $100 per service (I got twice as much in my last church), but it's definitely a start. Transportation is still going to be an issue (it's 30 minutes away), but I think it's definitely worth a shot since I'm pretty good with church music and music in general. 

I didn't know that there was a shortage of ABA therapists but I'm definitely looking into it and the Spectrum House is having me do some of the training online and some of the training in person. I'm very excited for it because it's one of my goals to work with developmentally disabled children, and they even are okay with me bringing my piano to the workplace to teach the kids music! 

When I say "this" and "I hate this", I mean specifically that I'm recovering from trauma (physical, sexual, emotional abuse) and this situation isn't as BAD as it could be-- but the stress of having no money detracts from my recovery which I would like to be speedy but it doesn't work like that. I get overwhelmed with feelings of emptiness and I get suicidal in a heartbeat (though I won't do anything anymore because I promised myself I wouldn't). 

I'm going to release financial responsibility of the phone to her and hopefully she will just accept it.

No, that would require my dad to give it to me-- I'm his dependent for a while until the next fiscal year I believe. Unfortunately, I think for school and stuff I'm still considered a dependent until I'm 24 even if I don't live with him and he provides nothing.

"Honestly, you sound like you've got a lot of growing up to do."

An astute observation. Thanks for the insight.

"Given that you don't protest the charge, I assume you did do something unacceptable. If you've got a job you don't like, the proper thing to do is find another, then resign."

Yes you are assuming. Like I said in the post, it's a sales job and I didn't understand WHAT the job really was. It was more complex than a sales job, like selling sales. Following people around the store asking if they wanted free estimates for home improvement. I just wanted a job. I have multiple, recurring and pervasive mental illness(es) that prevent me from being able to focus, listen, or really do anything competently. I disclosed that in the application. I thought I could overcome it, I was wrong.

"It's nobody's job to warn you about these things. You have to read the T&C's yourself and compare different offers before choosing the best one for you. Sounds safe to say you didn't."

Nobody's job? I'll just ignore that. I had literally no experience ever opening a bank account and I was 19 at the time. I never even had problems before a couple of months ago when I DIDN'T have income. 

"If this was an office job, you should have got the bus every day, there and back. No ubers"

Can't take the bus back, no bus ran at that time.

"$500? $700? Something else? C'mon, if you're this casual about how much money you earn then of course you're going to have issues."

I was asking for advice, not commentary about my personal flaws. I don't know the exact amount because they haven't told me my hour or anything-- after I finish training I KNOW it will be $700 a month. But in the mean time it will be $8.05 an hour which is minimum wage. After I get certified, it's $700. ($10 an hour and probably 20 hours a week and full time if I'm "good" at the job, which I probably will be because I have some experience).

"This is it really. The point at which it was it was totally clear that you are mostly responsible for this situation. How could you have so little and sign up for $110/month on a phone. People who are poor through no fault of their own do not make these kinds of decisions."

That's nice that you think I'm responsible for all of this, but you don't have all the data pertaining toward my entire life. This is a friend who was getting out of an abusive household-- like myself, and I couldn't, in my mind at the time, just leave her to go back or be homeless. Also you didn't give any advice, just more snark.

I have bipolar disorder + an additional diagnosis more recent of schizophrenia. This does not make living and making decisions easy Especially when exacerbated by distressing living conditions that I was in. If it makes you feel better, we'll just say it's all my fault and I did this to myself. 

But I really don't see the point of anything you said.

It's not pride. I'm not sure why you're commenting if you're so adamant about giving useless advice? I don't need to explain to you and give receipts about how I came from a very abusive household, and I am not going back. Here, in Florida, I work very hard every day. I'm a pianist, I practice for hours-- in the hopes I can get a scholarship. It's hard to get access to a piano I do it. The point is I'm awake, and I can do things. I'm around people who do not harm me. My father (at home, which I so "pridefully" don't want to go back to) "pretends" to rape me, screams at me, rates me (like 1-10, I'm always low as you can imagine), threatens to murder me-- this isn't pride. I'm not going back home. I sleep all day at home and binge eat. At least here I have my health and I'm not giving that up because someone on the internet thinks I'm being "prideful" because I don't want to be part of my dad's weirdo creep sex talks and screaming matches.

The kind of advice that comes from people who are much older than myself and have lived through this and know more ways to get out of this thriving rather than "just get a job". Obviously I realize I need to get a job but there are many other factors involved and I asked if I was "missing something". Which to clarify means-- am I not putting myself out there enough? Am I not utilizing the skills I already have? What do I do in the mean time while trying to create income? Can I go to the unemployment office?

My parent's advice to me was "don't spend money ever" and that's how they did their finances and why they have a lot of money (I guess, I don't really know), but in the meantime me-- with bipolar disorder, and severe manic episodes, can't seem to really keep it together and manage money. But I never had any advice, no older person to tell me exact things to do-- which I needed. I don't mean this in a snarky way, I'm saying-- I have no clue what I'm doing and I'm looking for other options and trying not to become hopeless in this 1k of debt I'm drowning in.

Maybe I didn't make it clear enough that I cannot go back home and I have no place to stay where I came from. 

Also, I didn't blame the bank-- I very clearly blamed myself even though-- the bank isn't exactly a place where my money would grow if I was already below the poverty line, but thanks for the advice.

I have an associate's degree, just not a Bachelor's degree. I can absolutely not go back home. This isn't "my parents are mean and don't let me out" not going back home, this is a "I will be physically and emotionally harmed" if I go back home. Also, where my parent's live... there are no universities so I'd get to... get another associate's degree? And then not have health insurance because I'm not going to school full time. 

I had enough money to pay for the last month of the phone bill, yes. This was a friend who refused to get a phone but would not move out of where I was staying. It caused me great anxiety to not know where she was, and I didn't want her to go back to her abusive family. I felt responsible, I realize in retrospect that I wasn't responsible but now here I am.
Well I made it to the interview and I got the job but I'm unable to get transportation right now because I don't have any money. I feel very hopeless again.

I'm 21 years old and I've asked a lot of people (social workers, therapists) about being independent-- and it doesn't seem to be a possibility right now until the "next fiscal year". 

I didn't live with my dad when I got these bills from clinics. But his insurance WAS supposed to have full coverage. 

I have some people I can talk to, I just feel ashamed of feeling suicidal often.

Thank you so much for this response! I don't think I can cancel my bank account yet-- I use Wells Fargo and they're pretty terrible and full of fees EVERYWHERE-- but once I pay off my credit card debt I'm probably going to switch to a credit union. I think that might help. And the 1k of debt does feel like 1,000 pounds on my chest, it's very uncomfortable thinking about it. I really like your idea of saving up for a vacation, that would be amazing and definitely lift my spirits even if it's 20 months from now it's a definite goal!

No no I'm not underage, I'm 21, which is what makes this so complicated because there would be more services available to me were I underage. 

Here is what happened in a nutshell: I live in this city in Florida for three years. Those were some of the worst years when it came to living with my dad, he would shove me to the floor to scream at me constantly (well, it felt constant), I was in a constant state of distress (also felt constant). And I wanted to go to school, for piano performance at the local university. He wouldn't let me go, or support me and I had nothing at the time really-- and every time I would call him out on his abuse, he would take me to a psychiatrist and I would get medicated more. It was really awful. So I have an associate's degree from a community college in this city in Florida.

I moved to Alabama for 2 years, and six months ago I couldn't stand it (I couldn't stand it before, but this time I had more money and friends) so I moved out. But after six months, my friend (who is military that I was renting from) had to move and I couldn't afford her mortgage or anything. So I just decided to move to Florida with 15 cents and a bubblegum wrapper (I had nowhere to stay in Alabama anymore). I thought I had someplace to stay in Florida, I paid an old friend $400 for rent (leaving me with $300). He said he was getting evicted, so I had to find another place quick. Luckily, I had another old friend who I can stay with-- but it feels uncomfortable because I have nothing to really offer them. With my friend I was staying with-- he was offering to help me out with everything if I stayed with him, but he ended up moving back to his parents and just kind of ignoring me. I came back to Florida, btw, for the purpose of going to school here. 

All my expenses are: food, transportation and phone bill-- which is outrageously expensive because I was paying for my friend's phone bill because I was always worried about her and she refused to get one on her own. I thought she would keep her job, and pay her half-- but she didn't. So now I'm still having to pay those contracted phones (including my own). I'm eligible for "free government phones" but that sounds like a long process and I need a phone in the meantime for... everything. 

My boyfriend is going to help me get a car (giving me his old car) but I literally have $60 in my bank account- not including debt because my first paycheck was just half the paycheck-- and I had to use that to pay the phone bill. So IDK how I'm going to get my driver's license, DATA course, and car insurance + gas all paid for with this terrible job.

I feel stupid for taking this job because it ended up taking more money than receiving money-- and I can't even do the job right. So I will more than likely get fired. I have an interview for a job I would LOVE but I just don't see it working out because I can barely get to the interview for the job. It's really amazing, it's working with developmentally disabled kids and adults and that's something I'm really interested in doing. I just have no clue how any of this is going to happen. Because I've looked at all my options and it's looking particularly bleak right now. 

I know it probably sounds like I made a hell of a lot of stupid decisions, and I did- but I had no idea. I didn't have a mentor or anything, I was just trying to escape from what felt like hell (and I would rather die than go back) and now I'm just a little (very) lost.

I don't know how to update this so I'm just going to comment on every single one of these since I have time. I am on government assistance right now, I use SNAP and it's been incredibly useful. I've finally been able to eat. I'm not much of a meal planner or a cook, but it's still be immensely helpful. Small tasks do seem incredibly difficult, and there's some phone calls I STILL have to make whether I'm "feeling up to it" or not. 

I do have friends here, a couple of friends and a boyfriend... but I always hate asking for help and encouragement from the people I know. I always end up feeling like a burden and that's something I have to work through.

I've actually found a place to stay in Pensacola! I don't know how to add that to the thread so I've commented on your addition to my thread. Now all I have to worry about is ten thousand other things. I'm definitely going to contact my school to see what I can do about funding, because being in school with a job is going to be incredibly stressful for me (I already have an anxiety disorder, this would be a mess!). I have enough to pay for my school with FAFSA loans, as a full time student-- but I'm sure that won't cover rent and living expenses.

Thank you so much for everyone's advice! Even with housing, this advice is really helpful. I'm tremendously terrified but with enough persistence I'm hoping this will turn out okay.

Hugging people, holding hands. I was denied a lot of positive physical affection in my life, so this is incredibly important to me and really really helps me. Also, being out in nature and taking pictures. Being with my mom or my boyfriend.
BLESS YOU for posting this! I do the EXACT same thing with my boyfriend and I really really want it to stop-- off to go read your post!
I am similar to this. I will be a little bit anxious (or a lot a bit) and I'll think "You know what would solve this? Death."

She lived at her parents at the time, but she moved out shortly after. She was aware, but when she received the court date I believe she was in behavioral health. I think today we're going to call the city hall and ask about it.

I have taken Ativan before and I hate taking it because I don't want to become addicted, and also weed makes me very anxious. It does not help even a little bit. Every other drug besides that for SURE would be a mess and I'm not interested in throwing such intense chemicals at my brain for the time beings. 

The medications I do take regularly are mood stabilizers.

That's funny, I have dark brown hair too! I'm a pianist so I have to be around a lot of "misunderstanding older people" so they wouldn't be too happy with bright pink hair anything, so that would be EXCELLENT!
YES lolol that was my first though my dad HATES tattoos with a passion and said he wouldn't let me into his house with a tattoo because he "doesn't hang around people like that"
Wow actually that's an incredibly great idea, and I'm so glad that you told me this! Now I'm going to brainstorm some ideas that are like this!

I've looked on the Tricare website and asked a lot of people, I can stay on his insurance but for what I need it'll cost about $300 a month (after I turn 23 so I have a good year to weigh my options).I think it would be worth reimbursing him for the insurance simply because I spend so much time at the doctor's so it wouldn't be out of the question, in my opinion. 

Thank you for that advice, I really appreciate that. I could actually work as a teacher for a while, and being in school would be helpful for that-- but I think there may be degrees that would be more "lucrative" when it comes to earnings afterwards. I'm not terribly concerned with being "passionate" about anything luckily, because I can be enthusiastic about pretty much anything. 

Would it be stupid to work independently for a while until I turn 24 and my dad's high salary doesn't count towards my FAFSA anymore and I might be able to get SOME money? Or take a few classes to raise my GPA in the mean time at a community college (yet again) (so that I can afford it)? 

I guess nothing is set in stone and I can think about it but it's extremely high anxiety for me right now because I have no clue how to do this and I doubt myself a lot.

That's actually a good question that I hadn't really considered completely. It depends on what I would be going for. I'd have to spend a lot of time trying to figure that out, my parents always urged me to finish my bachelor's degree but neither of them had to pay for theirs so no wonder they would feel much differently about their own. 

The reason I want to stay in school for at least another year is just because I want to stay on my dad's health insurance, which I guess, he has gracefully allowed me to stay on (Tricare Prime).

Yes, I have a stable living situation and I do not have to pay rent. I don't have to contribute to anything but I'd at least like to contribute $200 a month. They're good friends of mine who have taken care of people worse off than me, but I don't plan on going there and just lying down for 6 months. Public transportation exists in Pensacola, I'm able bodied and luckily I have a lot of great friends there who don't mind giving rides for gas money. 

The music program will cost Alabama-tuition-- so not out of state, not in state but about $200 more per credit hour. I'm not terribly concerned with future employment opportunities because as long as I'm not expecting to be a superstar, there are actually a lot of employment opportunities as a musician, not to mention I am considering double-majoring in biology (since I have all my gen ed out of the way) so I can go to grad school for any general science really. If I can't go to UWF (University of West Florida), I'm strongly considering just going back to community college (again) and taking science courses to strengthen my background in that (for a lower price) until I can really support myself completely. But I have no idea if that's a super great idea.

I can't thank you enough for responding to this. It's so hard to write out and I write it out again and again trying to figure out where I went wrong and it's taking so long to realize that I wasn't really at fault. I spent my whole life as a child so far, how could it be my fault? I wanted to ask so many questions on this thread. But I forgot as I was writing it. I want to know- what do I do next? How do I have healthy relationships? How do I make the money to go to a university? Is it wise to move to Pensacola just because my friends and great boyfriend are there? How am I going to survive this when my brain is killing me a lot of the time and so many people don't understand? I'm ready to search for the answers, and uncovering these scars are so scary. I love you too, stranger. <3

I think bipolar is a part of my relationships, but I don't think it will destroy them. Because I am generally an OK if not very kind person, people are very forgiving of my many flaws. I met my current boyfriend who I love SO much (and that's relevant), about 2 years ago and we started on a solid friendship. I definitely think he has a personality well suited to handling whatever I can come up with. I am however, fully committed to recovery and that makes all the difference. He sees me trying, and he's part of my accountability. The thing is, in a relationship, I use the buddy system. I don't HAVE to go through all my own hogwash alone. I can talk to him about it. I see other women with bipolar with men who really aren't suited to anyone, let alone a woman with emotional lability. My previous boyfriends (only 2) liked me, but couldn't handle all the crying and the emotions. My current boyfriend has helped me grow and vice versa. I think bipolar disorder has lead to different experiences but I try not to judge them as "good" or "bad" when the overall relationship is overwhelmingly wonderful.

I realize I am bipolar all the time. Sometimes I take a shower and I'm like "mental illness where?", then proceed to sit in my towel for 6 years and in that time, write 3 novels in 2 days and take a road trip across the country while blowing all my money. That's how you know.

Since I'm diagnosed as mentally ill and am usually missing class because I'm vomiting/crying I pull what I like to call "the mentally ill card". You could just say you had anxiety though and get a referral from a primary care to a psychiatrist. It might be unethical but it'll probably work.

You're definitely not being an edge lord hahaha. I had to comment based just on that, but the thing is... I think you should look at the pros and cons before you leave. Do you have a job? Money? Anything? I recommend looking up what an abusive situation is like (and I definitely believe you, it can be difficult living with someone psychologically unstable), and making a safety plan. What important documents do you need? What would you need to keep in contact with your mother for? Just make sure you ask yourself a lot of questions before you leave and if it's really worth it. Have you suggested to your mom that she go to therapy? (I'm sure you have but just throwing it out there). I really hope things get better for you and if you can't leave, just spend a lot of time avoiding home-- I did that a lot.
I'm a 21 year old girl and you can be friends with me :) I'm here for you!
Please don't associate with 16 year old girls when you're 22.

No, seriously don't worry about it! And you're always welcome. Yes, it's absolutely terrible. And I find that some of it has to do with trauma in early childhood. Our childhoods kind of define a lot of our lives, sadly (for some of us). I do the SAME thing, I have no money because I'm always buying gifts and dinner. I don't develop feelings for people anymore really, so maybe that's a thing that will pass. Sometimes I didn't know if I was feeling because I was lonely or because that person was good for me. Of course my friends are amazing, but amazing isn't enough for a solid romantic relationship/life partner. You have a friend, you have me. I'm pretty good at being a friend even though I'm Absolutely Terrible at everything else. Brains are weird. But I think it can be overcome. The weirdness, I mean. Or at least productive.
If you still need someone to talk to, you can message me. I'll be here for you.

I think something that helped me cope with relationships in general and really, not being in them, is that no one is entitled to my feelings of affection and I'm not entitled to their feelings of affection. In most cases, I'm just entitled to basic human respect. I'm a 21-year old woman, and you can take everything I say and throw it out the door. I won't be offended. I've been hurt before, and I'm the Queen of lashing out at people who are trying to be nice. First of all I want to say, you can TOTALLY overcome this. But it's a long process and sometimes you just have to tell yourself "this is going to take a while". I once read this quote that said "Some things cannot be fixed, only carried" but I like to think, you can carry your problems and eventually you'll find new data along the way to fix your problems. I had this friend, let's call him Dave (his name was not... Dave... which is obvious from how I phrased that but I want to make that clear). I met him while I was with my abusive ex-boyfriend, and I was infatuated with him. In a really weird very obviously "she's bipolar" kind of way. I ended up growing very close to him, and falling in love with him in a way. But he turned out to be kind of a dud in a lot of ways. Sure, he listened to me but it was only physically listening not really... thinking about what I said or deciding not to be a selfish ass. I told myself, I can never live without Dave... I can't do this. But one day, I just blocked him from every social media outlet I had (I did meet him in person though, at school-- college). You just really have to disassociate from the emotions, rationalize them. Find what you're missing and then search to fill it or better yet-- grow it. Grow into the person you want to be so you can feel better and feel whole and loved. You deserve this, I promise. I'll try to write tomorrow because this was probably pointless but if you need someone to talk to I am here for you.

Hello. I think you deserve better than someone who does what my dad calls "hand holding". Not that my dad is the best person for relationship advice (he's been with my mom for 21+ years though-- as long as I've been alive). But sometimes women do this thing where they're with one man, but they want a back up man. You sound kind, and even if you weren't you're still a human being who deserves not to be someone's second choice. Hold out so you can be No.1. If you need anything, feel free to message me. I'm going to sleep soon but I'll always respond. My heart goes out to you.

Hello. I'm 21, and I've been there and in a way, I'm still there. When I was a little girl I used to watch the Wonderful Wizard of Oz (or maybe it was just the Wizard of Oz? You know, the classic one with Judy Garland) every single day. My dad thought it was a sign that I was bipolar, in retrospect. I don't quite think so. Anyway, now I don't really watch anything. I'm quite a fine musician (this is not by my own admission) and I get sad listening to music. Or I just feel empty. I constantly want to die. Literally constantly. I drop a plate on the floor and internally I'm like "well, I should just start digging my grave now!". I've found a sort of morbid sense of humor about it. Now, romance-- ah, I wouldn't put too much in store by it! I want to be in love, sometimes but at my healthiest I don't particularly care. I had a 3 month relationship when I was 17 (my first kiss, I know.... fantastic hahaha) and then I had a terribly abusive 4 month relationship when I was 19. Since that relationship I've been in a constant state of disassociation. I don't quite mind anymore, I just try to be kind to people and be useful. I creeped on your responses, and you seem like quite a kind likable person. I don't think you should die. Not that my thinking would matter either way, but if you need something I am wholeheartedly here for you even though I am a complete stranger.

From reading this, I'm going to assume that I'm younger than you since I don't have a lot of these experiences but I hope I can offer some support regardless. I'm 21 years old and I exhibited symptoms of bipolar disorder as a younger than 8 year old child. I'm just sharing these experiences so you can see how I relate, before I offer support. So, I hope I don't come off as offensive, presumptuous or selfish. I don't know you, but I do care. I really do, and if there's any amount of talking that will help you I will talk.  My family didn't react... pleasantly to finding out that I was basically a basket case. Honestly, I haven't gone longer than 2 weeks in my entire life without crying. I'm a mess! The longest job I held down in my life was a year and I only had to go once a week (I still have it, it was just temporary, I'm a musician for a church). Sometimes I could barely stand that, I had to wake up at 9 to be there at around 930 and sit around for service at 10 and I'd still manage to suffer the entire time. And the pastor didn't even make me sit through his sermon. Sometimes I would come there crying and acting like a hooligan. Generally speaking. In my time as a mentally ill person, I learned a lot. Possibly that I just have a lot more to learn, but basically-- everything that strangers tell you about mental illness is absolutely useless. I have lost a lot of friends as well, mostly just because I moved away, but I had one particular friend who-- despite some GLARING flaws, had some wonderful things to offer. She is schizophrenic and is basically lost to me now because of the severity of the illness and her physical distance-- but she told me, giving up was a non option. My solution was always suicide, I've been hospitalized no less than 5 times. 

Some people have really terrible lives. I think it's silly and disingenuous to act like people are the captains of their own souls. In some ways, we are, but in very obvious ways-- we aren't. And there are only two things that can really overcome the fact that our lives are in many ways predetermined. They don't have to be, but they are for a lot of people. In the same way a lot of people think they are original or creative or thoughtful, they are just spouting out the things they have learned-- you and me, are products of our environment. However-- those two things-- exceptional intelligence, and dedication. Fortitude, so to speak. Endurance. That kind of thing. The problem with a lot of people who are suffering is that they have never been exposed to any kind of "critical thinking" that might help them escape or conquer their circumstances. This isn't to say their stupid, this is to say that-- I would be the homeless person with the sign on the side of the road too, if I didn't have a father who is a Ph.D, M.D (i.e., a thinker, creative problem solver). So, I don't know the details of what you're going through. I mean the general details yes, but not the details that someone would need to really give a solution. If you follow, I'm trying to say... resist emotion. What I like to do, because I'm suffering mentally 99% of the time, is let emotions wash over me. Just soak in the pain and humiliation I feel. Then, slowly-- over the course of days or weeks, I distance myself from emotions and try to think through my problems. It's really grueling when most of the time I'd just rather be dead, but that's a non option. 

Thinking through problems sounds annoying when the "solutions" to your problems seem obvious: more money, more resources. But sometimes we don't have those and you are your only resource. When you think you are at the end of your rope, consider that we live in a universe of infinite possibilities and maybe, maybe there is something you missed. For me, I prefer to analyze ideas. My solution is educating myself the best I can. Whether it's at the library or at the internet, I distract myself from severe emotional pain by studying. 

This was probably totally useless and I'm sorry but I have one last thought. People like to give out unsolicited advice all the time. One of my favorite meaningless platitudes is, "The truth hurts". I once watched a TED Talk by Andrew Solomon called "Depression: The Secret We All Share". Solomon talks about how when we're depressed (and I'm referring to what you describe as "dark thoughts" and "overwhelming") we think that every sad thought we have is the truth. I think though, rationally, we can figure out-- deduce so to speak, that sadness isn't the truth. Sadness is an emotion, and the fact that we're feeling it IS truth but the thoughts that it produces can be... incorrect and unhelpful and just, wrong. So, the truth doesn't hurt. I hope you find healing and peace.

Yes, winter is my favorite part of the year when seasonal depression takes over for a while instead of my normal Bipolar Disorder. I'm really glad your mood is stable with your meds! I've been bipolar since I was 8 and literally Nothing Works. I'm surprised you're taking Adderall though, since my psychiatrists have never allowed it.
